articles.title: ‘No doubt’: AB de Villiers makes fresh Australian ball-tampering claim
articles.summary: Former South Africa batter claims ball was doctored in first Test. ‘It started in Durban, not in Port Elizabeth,’ says De Villiers. AB de Villiers claims he is certain Australia tampered with the ball as far back as the first Test of their infamous 2018 series in South Africa.
body: The former South Africa batter was in the middle when Cameron Bancroft was caught by TV cameras using sandpaper in the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town.
Bancroft, Usman Khawaja and Chadd Sayers have all alleged sandpaper was used to tamper with the ball in the second Test at Gqerberha, formerly Port Elizabeth.
De Villiers set up South Africa’s six-wicket win in that Test to level the series at 1-1 with an unbeaten century in the first innings.
After biting his tongue during the unfolding drama, South Africa’s fourth highest Test run-scorer has entered the fray to say he has “no doubt” Australia’s premeditated cheating began even earlier.

articles.title: Mets reportedly agree $450m contract with Tarik Skubal, richest deal for pitcher in MLB history
articles.summary: Ace’s contract reportedly for nine years. Mets have missed playoffs for last two seasons. The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.
body: The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history. The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024.

The left-hander, a two-time Cy Young winner, is one of the best pitchers in baseball. He turned 30 last week, and had surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow in May, but was still a prized target for teams looking to contend in the coming seasons. He ​reportedly also met with ​the Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres and Los ​Angeles Dodgers.
Skubal’s agreement reportedly includes a full no-trade clause and a $45m signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season.

Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings. Over his seven-year major league career, Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA. Skubal made his MLB debut for the Detroit Tigers and remained at the club until he was traded to the Dodgers this summer.
points: Mets have missed playoffs for last two seasons.
The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.
The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history.
The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024.

articles.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
articles.summary: Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty. Atalanta snatch point in thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter. Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.
body: Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

articles.title: Gerwyn Price ends barren run with Grand Slam of Darts win: ‘Now they can stop talking’
articles.summary: Price beats Gian van Veen 16-11 to secure title. Welshman lost ‘so many finals’ in four years of pain. Gerwyn Price finally ended his major trophy drought by winning the Grand Slam of Darts and is delighted to silence his critics.
body: But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton. Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the fourth time, but this one will surely mean the most to him.

The 41-year-old, who swatted away a wasp and Kevin Doets in the semi-finals earlier on Sunday, was embroiled in a tense and nervy encounter which turned in the 15th leg. Van Veen had six darts to break for an 8-7 lead, but could not finish and Price seized the moment. He took out double two on his fifth attempt to win the leg and then reeled off the next six to take control.
It was an imperious period of play which left Van Veen with no way back as “the Iceman” coolly saw out the win to get back into the winners’ circle – his eighth major title.

His lack of silverware has been a talking point and he is happy to end the noise. “I was probably more nervous in this game than ever,” he said. “I’ve lost so many finals. Just to keep the media off my back, it’s not for me.
points: Price beats Gian van Veen 16-11 to secure title.
Gerwyn Price finally ended his major trophy drought by winning the Grand Slam of Darts and is delighted to silence his critics.

articles.title: Virginia Tech basketball: Hokies lose first game to Oklahoma State after terrible second half
articles.summary: The 6-0 Virginia Tech Hokies were back Sunday in the Shriners Children’s Charleston Classic in Charleston, South Carolina. The opponent: the Oklahoma State Cowboys. After a back-and-forth first half with the lead changing often, the Cowboys took control in the second half, outscoring the Hokies…
body: Remarkably, this game was tied at halftime. Both teams were hot from the field, with OSU shooting 59% and the Hokies 47% in the first half. Tech made 8-of-15 (53%) from beyond the arc in the first half, while the Cowboys made 5-of-10.

While the Hokies cooled off in the second half, Oklahoma State only got hotter. VT made only 11 of 28 field-goal attempts in the second half, including 4-for-14 from the 3-point line, while the Cowboys shot an unheard-of 74% in the second half. And there you have it, that’s the game.

The back-and-forth action from the first half carried into the second half. However, back-to-back buckets from Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry at the 16:31 mark gave the Hokies a 54-51 lead. The crowd sensed the tide might be turning in Virginia Tech’s favor. Instead, it spurred a run by the Cowboys that opened up the game. Oklahoma State scored the next 11 points to build an 8-point lead. The Cowboys never looked back.
After a Hammond 3-pointer and two Jaylen Curry free throws cut the lead back to 64-59, OSU scored 13 in a row to blow it wide open.

Tech made 8-of-15 (53%) from beyond the arc in the first half, while the Cowboys made 5-of-10.

body: Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he showed everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.
He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.
Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

articles.title: Mexican national anthem turns heads ahead of NFL game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings met at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday night, marking the NFL’s first regular-season game in Mexico since 2022. Before a single snap was played, though, the crowd made sure that the night would be remembered for more than just football.
body: As Mexican singer Majo Aguilar performed the Mexican national anthem, the entire stadium sang along with her in a moment that quickly went viral. Fans and media members alike were blown away, with many saying it gave them chills.

The NFL announced back in September that Aguilar would sing the Mexican national anthem, while Oakland-born singer-songwriter MXKA would perform the U.S. national anthem. Aguilar, a member of Mexico’s famed Aguilar music family and a cousin of Ángela Aguilar, has more than 533 million global streams and also sang the anthem as part of Telemundo’s World Cup coverage.

“I feel very happy to be able to perform the Mexican National Anthem. Mexico is a beautiful country with a rich culture,” Aguilar said in the NFL’s announcement. “Thank you to the NFL for inviting me to be part of such a special moment and allowing me to represent my country. It fills me with pride to be Mexican.”

Needless to say, she and the crowd delivered. Video of the performance shared by SportsCenter racked up more than 500,000 views within a couple of hours, and plenty of people chimed in with their reactions.

articles.title: Hojgaard shares PGA Tour lead as RSM Classic dragged into Monday finish
articles.summary: Rasmus Hojgaard holds a share of the lead heading into a weather-delayed final day of the RSM Classic, with England's Marco Penge in contention as he looks to secure his PGA Tour future.
body: Hojgaard entered the week 122nd in the FedExCup standings and among the players looking to break into the top 100 and remain fully exempt on the PGA Tour next season, with the Dane now in prime position to do that.

The Ryder Cup star posted a five-under 65 on the Seaside Course at Sea Island Golf Club, firing five birdies to move to 13 under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen, with Max Greyserman a shot off the pace in third.

The Dane carded back-to-back birdies from the sixth and followed a 10-foot birdie at the 12th by holing from 30 feet for another at the 16th, before closing a blemish-free day by draining a 25-footer at the par-four last to move joint-top of the leaderboard.

"Today felt very free - tomorrow's a completely different day," Hojgaard said. "I'm going to feel the nerves. I think that's what we all play for is to put ourselves in those positions, and we'll see what happens."

body: The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's first match in charge of United got off to a dreadful start as they had defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute and were 2-0 down by the 13th minute.
That left them with a mountain to climb, with Liverpool scoring twice more in the second half to secure a 4-0 win that kept United second from bottom in the table.
"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino of the situation that faced his new side after those woeful opening 13 minutes.
"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?

articles.title: Jamaica level series with dominant win over England
articles.summary: England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena.
body: A day on from a dramatic 47-46 victory in the series opener at the same London venue, England were second-best as the Sunshine Girls claimed a comfortable victory and levelled the four-Test series.

The visitors scored six consecutive points on their way to opening a 15-7 advantage after the first quarter, then the Commonwealth Games silver medallists extended their lead to 11 points by half-time.
A tight third quarter saw Jamaica edge further ahead, with the Sunshine Girls never relinquishing their advantage as they closed out a convincing win on away soil.
"We expected Jamaica to come out hard and they certainly did deliver on that," England coach Anna Stembridge admitted.
